1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nf6.name: Sicilian Defence: Nimzowitsch Variation
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nf6.background: Named after Aron Nimzowitsch, who pioneered it as one of two provocative variations of the Sicilian Defence; it is also known as the Nimzowitsch–Rubinstein Variation. After 3.e5 Nd5 it resembles Alekhine's Defence.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.e5.strategy: Chases the knight at once and gains space. Black must spend a second move on the same piece, and White's pawn on e5 cramps Black's development, though it also has to be supported against attack in the fight that follows.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.e5.name: Sicilian Defence: Nimzowitsch Variation, Advance Variation

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nc3.strategy: A flexible alternative: it defends e4 against the knight and keeps d4 in reserve, steering for a normal Open Sicilian. White gives up the space-gaining but committal e5 advance, so the game is less sharp and Black has an easy time finding a sound set-up.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nc3.name: Sicilian Defence: Nimzowitsch Variation, Closed Variation

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.e5 Nd5.strategy: Puts the knight on the best square available: it is central and nothing attacks it yet, and from there it eyes c3, b4 and f4. Black has lost time, but White's advanced e5 pawn now needs support, and the fight for the centre goes on.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nc3 d6.strategy: Stops e4-e5, which would hit the knight again, and prepares to meet d4 by capturing. Black heads for a standard Open Sicilian with the pawn on d6 and a knight on f6, and avoids the cramped games that the e5 advance gives.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.e5 Nd5 4.Nc3.strategy: Develops with a threat to trade off the centralised knight. White gains another tempo and keeps the extra space, so Black must decide whether to trade or to support the knight.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.e5 Nd5 4.Nc3 e6.strategy: Supports the knight with a pawn, so that a trade on d5 can be answered by recapturing with the pawn instead of the queen, and opens the f8 bishop. Black accepts a recapture that leaves a pawn on d5 against White's advanced e5 and fights for the centre from a solid base.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.e5 Nd5 4.Nc3 Nxc3.name: Sicilian Defence: Nimzowitsch Variation, Exchange Variation
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.e5 Nd5 4.Nc3 Nxc3.strategy: Trades the strong knight for White's, and White recaptures with a developing pawn move that opens lines for the queen and the c1 bishop. Black has spent time, while the e5 pawn goes on cramping Black's game. Playable, but the main route is better.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.e5 Nd5 4.Nc3 e6 5.Nx.strategy: Removes Black's most active piece; Black normally recaptures with the pawn. White keeps the e5 pawn as a cramping spearhead and prepares to strike at the centre at once.
The natural recapture: Black gets pawns on c5 and d5 against White's e5 and a share of the centre, but those pawns will be under pressure.
Strikes at once at Black's pawn centre: the pawn attacks c5 and backs up e5, so the white centre is firm. White opens the game while Black's pieces are still at home, and play becomes sharp.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.e5 Nd5 4.Nc3 e6 5.Nx.name: Sicilian Defence: Nimzowitsch Variation, Main Line
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.e5 Nd5 4.Nc3 e6 5.Nx.strategy: Develops with pressure on both d4 and e5, so the centre is tested at once while the pawns on c5 and d5 stay in place. The result is a sharp struggle, in which White tends to keep the better chances.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nc3 d6 4.d4.strategy: Opens the centre, trading White's central pawn for Black's c-pawn. White gets space and open lines for the pieces, and the game reaches a main line of the Open Sicilian by a different route.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nc3 d6 4.d4 cxd4.strategy: Takes the pawn and trades a wing pawn for a central one, the heart of every Open Sicilian: Black gets a half-open c-file and a healthy central majority, White gets space and a lead in development.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nc3 d6 4.d4 cxd4 5.N.strategy: Recaptures with the knight, which now dominates the centre. The game is a standard Open Sicilian, where White has more space and Black a sound structure with counterplay on the c-file.
